reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a step-by-step ETH flash-loan arbitrage process that asks viewers to connect MetaMask and send ETH to a deployed contract. It promotes the funded contract as a repeatable way to make money, and the description claims that retrying with specified parameters should work 100% and produce profit. The interface shows a 0.1 ETH send, although the records do not establish the recipient's control, contract behavior, recoverability of funds, or any completed profit.

citations.quote: 2023 Uniswap Arbitrage Bot Code For Flash Loan Arbitrage Using ETH
Step By Step Tutorial for Flash Loan:
Connect your MetaMask wallet.
Send ETH to
the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.05 ETH

opening.argument: Judge, the instructions acknowledge that the process can fail: the description says arbitrage may fail as gas prices vary, and it warns against using amounts below the stated threshold. It also tells viewers to move their ETH out afterward. Those cautions do not prove the contract is sound, but they make the presentation more consistent with a risky technical procedure than an unconditional promise of returns.

citations.quote: Under some very rare cases, the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of ETH in your smart contract as gas price varies from time to time.
Avoid using very low amounts as contract may fail below 0.05 ETH.
Make sure to transfer your ETH out to another wallet when you're done.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that viewers are told to fund a contract, but funding is presented as necessary to run it, with gas costs offered as the explanation. The opening does not establish who controls the recipient or whether viewers can recover funds. The stated failure conditions deserve weight alongside the funding instruction.

citations.quote: You're going to have to send gas money to run this contract
Under some very rare cases, the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of ETH in your smart contract as gas price varies from time to time.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cautions are narrow and are followed by advice to send more ETH if the process fails. The same description claims a retry with specified settings should work 100% and yield profit. A warning about variable gas prices does not neutralize that assurance or the instruction to fund the deployed contract.

citations.quote: Note: if it doesn't work with 0.05 ETH try to send another 0.05 ETH (0.2 is better), because fees may be different from day to day.
retry the transaction this time preferably with 825 loan amount and 31,560 gas limit and it should work 100% but with a smaller profit.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the recording is a software walkthrough. The speaker explains creating a Solidity file in Remix, selecting a compiler version, deploying a contract and choosing constructor inputs. The token name and symbol are described as arbitrary. That detailed, reproducible sequence supports reading the video as an operational demonstration, even though its claims about profitable arbitrage should be treated skeptically.

citations.quote: You're going to create a new file and call it flashloan.sol.
And this is the compiler version. And we're actually using 050. So we're going to have to change this.
You can make up any token name. This is going to be a dummy token and then we're gonna the token symbol that can be anything.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes sending ETH, but that step appears within a longer deployment and execution walkthrough. Its evidence establishes an instruction to fund a newly deployed contract, not what the contract actually does or whether the depicted wallet result is a completed profit. The technical demonstration remains a plausible reading of what is shown.

citations.quote: Step By Step Tutorial for Flash Loan:
Click on the "Solidity Compiler" and set the compiler version to 0.5.0
the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.05 ETH

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial format does not make the funding instruction incidental. Viewers are directed to obtain contract code from a linked site, send ETH to the deployed contract and execute its action. The speaker then presents the result as something viewers can repeat to make money. Those are operational instructions coupled to a return claim, not merely an explanation of Solidity controls.

citations.quote: Smart Contract Code: www.get-flashloan.com/smart-code-0-5-0-eth/
the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.05 ETH
And you can do this all day long. So I hope you, hopefully you liked my video and hopefully it makes you money.

opening.argument: Judge, the record supports caution, but it does not establish the decisive mechanics of a diversion. The speaker says the contract is tied to the address used to launch it and that the viewer controls it. The instructions tell viewers to copy the address of their newly deployed contract before sending ETH. Neither statement verifies the code or guarantees withdrawal, but the supplied material does not show that the ETH is sent to a creator-controlled wallet or that recovery is impossible. The funding step alone should not settle those questions.

citations.quote: It's actually going to be locked into that address you're launching from. You have complete control over it.
Copy the address of the newly deployed contract.
the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.05 ETH

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution fairly identifies a request to send ETH and an aggressive profit claim. Yet its opening also concedes that recipient control, contract behavior and recoverability are not established. Those unknowns matter: a send to a contract the viewer has just deployed cannot, on this record alone, be equated with a demonstrated transfer to the speaker.

citations.quote: Copy the address of the newly deployed contract.
You have complete control over it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker's assertion of viewer control is not verification of the contract's behavior. Viewers are directed to paste code from an external site, fund the deployed contract and, if the attempt fails, send more ETH. The record need not prove the ultimate recipient to show that the video promotes funding an unverified contract through promises of arbitrage returns.
